## Load Libraries and Data

```{r load-libraries}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(viridis)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

# Load the student-week aggregations
data <- read_csv("student_week_aggregations2.csv")

# Basic data info
cat("Data dimensions:", nrow(data), "rows,", ncol(data), "columns\n")
cat("Date range:", min(data$week_id), "to", max(data$week_id), "\n")
cat("Number of unique students:", n_distinct(data$anon_student_id), "\n")
cat("Number of unique weeks:", n_distinct(data$week_id), "\n")
```

## Helper Functions for Visualizations

```{r helper-functions}
# Function to create heatmaps for any metric
create_heatmap <- function(data, metric_col, title_suffix, sample_size = 20) {
  # Filter to students with data for the metric and reasonable activity
  students_with_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
  group_by(anon_student_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_weeks = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_weeks >= 3)  # At least 3 weeks of data

  # Sample students for heatmap
set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
  sample_size <- min(sample_size, nrow(students_with_data))
  sampled_students <- students_with_data %>%
  slice_sample(n = sample_size) %>%
  pull(anon_student_id)

# Prepare data for heatmap
heatmap_data <- data %>%
  filter(anon_student_id %in% sampled_students,
           !is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
  mutate(student_label = paste0("S", match(anon_student_id, sampled_students)))

# Create heatmap
  p <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = week_id, y = student_label, fill = !!sym(metric_col))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", metric_col)), 
                       option = "plasma",
                       na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(
      title = paste("Student", title_suffix, "Heatmap Across Weeks"),
    subtitle = paste("Sample of", length(sampled_students), "students"),
    x = "Week",
    y = "Student"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
  )

  return(list(plot = p, sampled_students = sampled_students))
}

# Function to create line plots for any metric
create_line_plot <- function(data, metric_col, title_suffix, sampled_students) {
  # Prepare data for line plot
  line_data <- data %>%
    filter(anon_student_id %in% sampled_students,
           !is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
    mutate(student_label = paste0("S", match(anon_student_id, sampled_students)))
  
  p <- ggplot(line_data, aes(x = week_id, y = !!sym(metric_col), color = student_label, group = student_label)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Student", option = "plasma") +
  labs(
      title = paste("Student", title_suffix, "Progression Over Time"),
    subtitle = paste("Sample of", length(sampled_students), "students"),
    x = "Week",
      y = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", metric_col))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 2)))

  return(p)
}

# Function to create box plots for any metric
create_box_plot <- function(data, metric_col, title_suffix, log_scale = FALSE) {
  # Filter to weeks with sufficient data
weekly_counts <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
  count(week_id, name = "n_students") %>%
  filter(n_students >= 5)  # At least 5 students per week

box_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(metric_col)),
         week_id %in% weekly_counts$week_id)

  p <- ggplot(box_data, aes(x = week_id, y = !!sym(metric_col))) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = week_id), 
               outlier.alpha = 0.6, 
               outlier.size = 0.8,
               fill = "lightblue", 
               alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), 
              method = "loess", 
              se = TRUE, 
              color = "red", 
              size = 1) +
  labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of Student", title_suffix, "Across Weeks"),
    subtitle = "Box plots show quartiles, red line shows trend",
    x = "Week",
      y = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", metric_col))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
    )
  
  # Apply log scale if requested
  if (log_scale) {
    p <- p + scale_y_log10()
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# Function to generate summary statistics
generate_summary_stats <- function(data, metric_col, title_suffix) {
  # Overall statistics
  overall_summary <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
      mean_value = mean(!!sym(metric_col)),
      median_value = median(!!sym(metric_col)),
      sd_value = sd(!!sym(metric_col)),
      min_value = min(!!sym(metric_col)),
      max_value = max(!!sym(metric_col))
  )

  cat("Overall", title_suffix, "Statistics:\n")
  print(overall_summary)

# Weekly trend summary
weekly_summary <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(metric_col))) %>%
  group_by(week_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_students = n(),
      mean_value = mean(!!sym(metric_col)),
      median_value = median(!!sym(metric_col)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(week_id)

  cat("\nWeekly", title_suffix, "Summary (first 10 weeks):\n")
  print(head(weekly_summary, 10))
  
  return(list(overall = overall_summary, weekly = weekly_summary))
}
```

## Proficiency Analysis

```{r proficiency-analysis}
heatmap_result <- create_heatmap(data, "avg_proficiency", "Proficiency")
print(heatmap_result$plot)

line_plot <- create_line_plot(data, "avg_proficiency", "Proficiency", heatmap_result$sampled_students)
print(line_plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)))

box_plot <- create_box_plot(data, "avg_proficiency", "Proficiency")
print(box_plot + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)))

proficiency_stats <- generate_summary_stats(data, "avg_proficiency", "Proficiency")
```

## Minutes Per Week Analysis

```{r minutes-analysis}
heatmap_result <- create_heatmap(data, "minutes_per_week", "Minutes Per Week")
print(heatmap_result$plot)

line_plot <- create_line_plot(data, "minutes_per_week", "Minutes Per Week", heatmap_result$sampled_students)
print(line_plot)

# Use log scale for minutes due to wide range
box_plot <- create_box_plot(data, "minutes_per_week", "Minutes Per Week", log_scale = TRUE)
print(box_plot + labs(subtitle = "Box plots show quartiles, red line shows trend (log scale)"))

minutes_stats <- generate_summary_stats(data, "minutes_per_week", "Minutes Per Week")
```

## Correlation Analysis

```{r correlation-analysis}
# Create correlation matrix for all metrics
correlation_data <- data %>%
  select(avg_proficiency, minutes_per_week, problems_solved, total_opportunities) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

cor_matrix <- cor(correlation_data)

# Create correlation heatmap using tidyr
cor_melted <- cor_matrix %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Var1, names_to = "Var2", values_to = "value")

p_cor <- ggplot(cor_melted, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", 
                       midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1), space = "Lab", 
                       name="Correlation") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), color = "black", size = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Matrix of Student Weekly Metrics",
    x = "", y = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )

print(p_cor)

cat("Correlation Matrix:\n")
print(round(cor_matrix, 3))
```
